messages:
tariq: Heads-up: found a reproducible oddity in the Rust SDK/sample app during onboarding. Batching 12 items to /embeddings -> most embeddings are 512 but 1-2 occasionally come back as 128. Seems correlated with retry/backoff when auth refresh happens.
emily: interesting. which runtime/model and which SDK commit?
tariq: model=redwood-embed-1 (512d). Rust SDK at commit a1b2c3, sampleapp uses hyper + connection pooling. Repro: send batch, simulate token expiry at ~50ms after request start, let SDK refresh and retry. Intermittently one item has vec len 128 in the parsed response. Raw response chunk shows full floats but parsed vector is shorter.
vijay: could be buffer reuse or a serde/read boundary issue in the streaming parser. If the parser reuses an internal Vec without clearing or uses unsafe slice trick, previous capacity might show truncated length.
tariq: raw response excerpt (sanitized):
```
{"data":[{"id":0,"embedding":[...512 floats...]},{"id":1,"embedding":[...128 floats...]},...],"model":"redwood-embed-1"}
```
emily: hmm. Unlike other cases where different model dims appear, here server reported same model. So either server mutated output (unlikely) or SDK parsing munged it. Did you repro on Python/Node SDK?
tariq: Node + Python sampleapps do not exhibit this exact 128 truncation pattern. They showed mixed 384 vs 512 in other threads, but here Rust is special. I suspect a pooling+parser edge where when retry replaces connection the streaming read returns an earlier chunk which our parser interprets as a complete embedding but only reads first N floats because of a length field read bug.
vijay: actionable fixes: 1) add strict length validation in Rust SDK after parsing JSON; 2) make the streaming parser own freshly-allocated Vecs per item instead of reusing; 3) on auth-refresh retries, explicitly close the underlying connection or disable reuse for the retried request.
tariq: I drafted a small fix: rust-sdk#78 - after parse check: for item in response.data { if item.embedding.len() != model_dim { return Err(EmbeddingShapeMismatch{ expected: model_dim, found: item.embedding.len() }); } } Also added tracing span for "embedding_dim_mismatch".
emily: good. Also open a runtime issue: if server sees inconsistent lengths in a single response body, it should return a 500 with a clear diagnostic. Server-side check prevents polluted data reaching clients.
ci-bot: created issue RT-10234 (runtime: verify embedding vector lengths per-response)
vijay: extra test: add a fuzz test where we simulate partial chunk boundaries and ensure parser doesn't produce truncated vectors. Also run the sampleapp under a heavy 401-in-the-middle load to ensure fix is robust.
tariq: added unit + integration tests. Local run: 1000 iterations forcing expiry -> before fix 9 truncations, after fix parser/resolver surfaced 9 errors (caught) and no silent truncations. With connection-close-on-retry applied -> 0 truncations.
emily: for DX: add a short note in onboarding docs explaining that if users see "short" embeddings they should upgrade Rust SDK to >=x.y.z and that this can surface when token refresh occurs mid-batch.
doc-bot: added changelog entry and troubleshooting note: "If embeddings appear shorter than expected, upgrade SDK or disable connection reuse on retry" (PR queued).
vijay: longer term: add server header "X-embedding-dim" and include model name in response metadata so clients can pre-validate before parsing heavy arrays. Also consider switching to newline-delimited JSON for streaming items to simplify boundary handling.
tariq: filing follow-ups: rust-sdk#79 (parser memory ownership), runtime RT-10234, docs PR linked.
ci-bot: CI queued for rust-sdk/shape-guard (#78) job 9912
emily: thanks for the thorough triage. Once CI is green and docs updated we'll ship the patch. Assigning owners: runtime=infra-team, rust-sdk=vijay, docs=doc-bot. Closing thread after green.
tariq: will post repro script in #devex for others to run locally. thanks all.
